      <title>Pinterest: Data Scientist II, Infrastructure</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> San Francisco, CA, US; Remote, US
</p>

<div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Pinterest:</strong></p>
<p>Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.</p>
<p>Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the&nbsp;<a href="https://www.pinterestcareers.com/our-life/pinflex/">flexibility</a> to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.</p>
<p>At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.</p>
<p>Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process <a href="https://www.pinterestcareers.com/our-philosophy-on-ai-in-hiring/">here</a>.</p></div><p>Pinterest brings millions of people the inspiration to create a life they love. Behind that experience is a complex infrastructure ecosystem that powers reliability, performance, measurement, and efficiency across the platform. As Pinterest grows, it’s increasingly important that we understand these systems clearly so we can make smarter decisions for both Pinners and the business.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p>We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Infrastructure Data Science team. In this role, you’ll partner with engineering and cross-functional teams to make Pinterest’s infrastructure more measurable, intelligible, and actionable. Depending on the area, your work may span app performance, shopping infrastructure, metrics quality, infrastructure governance, or site reliability. You’ll help build the data foundations, measurement systems, and analytical frameworks that enable Pinterest to optimize core technical systems and make better product and infrastructure decisions.<br><br></p>
<p><strong>What you’ll do:</strong></p>
<p>In this role, you will partner closely with engineering and cross-functional teams to improve how Pinterest measures, understands, and optimizes its infrastructure:</p>
<ul>
<li>Partner with engineering teams to define, measure, and improve the health, quality, and efficiency of Pinterest’s infrastructure systems.</li>
<li>Build and refine metrics, dashboards, and analytical frameworks that make complex technical systems more understandable and actionable.</li>
<li>Strengthen data foundations by improving metric definitions, auditing data quality, and contributing to pipeline and measurement improvements where needed.</li>
<li>Design and analyze experiments, investigations, and deep dives to quantify the impact of infrastructure changes on user experience, reliability, and business outcomes.</li>
<li>Translate ambiguous technical problems into clear analyses and actionable recommendations for engineering and platform partners.</li>
<li>Support high-priority investigations and decision-making related to infrastructure performance, reliability, cost, and measurement quality.</li>
<li>Identify opportunities to improve how Pinterest measures and optimizes infrastructure across a range of domains, such as performance, shopping infrastructure, governance, metrics quality, and site reliability.<br><br></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>What we’re looking for:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Masters degree in a relevant field such as Statistics, Applied Math, Biostatistics, or equivalent experience.</li>
<li>Strong SQL and analytical programming skills, with experience working through messy, imperfect data and building reliable metrics and datasets.</li>
<li>Experience partnering on or contributing to production-ready data pipelines, measurement systems, or foundational data work that improves data quality and usability.</li>
<li>Solid foundation in experimentation and measurement, with the ability to design analyses, interpret results rigorously, and partner effectively with engineers and other cross-functional stakeholders.</li>
<li>Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous problems into clear analytical workstreams and actionable recommendations.</li>
<li>Strong cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly to engineering, product, and platform stakeholders.</li>
<li>Ability to operate independently, prioritize across both longer-term projects and fast-turn inbound requests, and drive work forward in a dynamic environment.</li>
<li>Curiosity and a builder mindset, with excitement for improving messy systems and creating more scalable, trustworthy measurement foundations.</li>
</ul>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Relocation Statement:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p class="p1"><span class="s1">We recognize that the ideal environment for work is situational and may differ across departments. What this looks like day-to-day can vary based on the needs of each organization or role.</span></p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><span class="s1"><strong>In-Office Requirement Statement:</strong></span></p>
<ul>
<li>This position is not eligible for relocation assistance. Visit our<a href="https://www.pinterestcareers.com/pinflex/"> PinFlex</a> page to learn more about our working model.</li>
<li>
<p class="p1"><span class="s1">This role will need to be in the office for in-person collaboration 1-2 times/quarter and therefore can be situated anywhere in the country.</span></p>
</li>
</ul>

We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

The Stream Reporting team is responsible for capturing and processing the consumption signals that power some of Spotify’s most important experiences and business functions. Our systems help ensure accurate royalty reporting, support experimentation and analytics, and provide trusted data that informs recommendations and personalization across Spotify.

We’re looking for an Android Engineer to join a highly collaborative team working at the intersection of mobile development, data, and platform systems. This is an opportunity to build software that operates at Spotify scale and helps power experiences used by millions of listeners every day. You’ll help shape how listening and engagement signals are captured across Spotify’s mobile experiences and transformed into trusted datasets used throughout the company.

    The Audiobooks Mission is a team in the Product & Technology organisation focused on the ecosystem and strategies of Audiobooks on Spotify. We work across both the creator and consumer audiobooks ecosystems, in order to get the best possible product to market with the best possible content.

    Spotify's Audiobooks team is helping shape the future of audio storytelling by bringing the world's best audiobook experiences to millions of listeners. As Associate Manager, Audiobook Licensing & Author Partnerships, you'll play an important role in growing our catalog while building meaningful relationships across the independent publishing community.

    You'll work with entrepreneurial authors, hybrid publishers, independent presses, and distribution partners to identify great content, negotiate commercial partnerships, and help creators succeed on Spotify. We're building it in close collaboration with Google, on open standards, so that different kinds of data are queryable the same way and teams can bring the right engine, from BigQuery to Dataflow to Trino, to the job. The work has two parts. Hecate enables Iceberg for the Parquet datasets that already exist across Spotify, so teams get the benefits without rewriting their data. Alongside it, we're building the foundations of a new Lakehouse architecture that lets workflows write Iceberg tables natively. We're shipping the MVP this cycle, and you'll help shape what comes next. We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data. We're judged on reliability, cost efficiency and how quickly we unblock users when something breaks. This backend role sits where open table formats, cloud data warehouses and processing engines meet.   ","description":"

    LilEngine is leading the Lakehouse, a company-strategic effort to make Apache Iceberg a first-class citizen in Spotify's data ecosystem. We're building it in close collaboration with Google, on open standards, so that different kinds of data are queryable the same way and teams can bring the right engine, from BigQuery to Dataflow to Trino, to the job.

    The work has two parts. Hecate enables Iceberg for the Parquet datasets that already exist across Spotify, so teams get the benefits without rewriting their data. Alongside it, we're building the foundations of a new Lakehouse architecture that lets workflows write Iceberg tables natively. We're shipping the MVP this cycle, and you'll help shape what comes next.

    We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data. We're judged on reliability, cost efficiency and how quickly we unblock users when something breaks. This backend role sits where open table formats, cloud data warehouses and processing engines meet.

     

    ","id":"926149ab-6999-4058-b35d-41e302b70e05","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Build and evolve the lakehouse: Help build the foundations that let data workflows read and write Iceberg tables directly, from this cycle's MVP to a production-grade platform.
  • Drive adoption: Help migrate data pipelines from across Spotify onto the new stack, making the move as painless as possible through tooling, standards and hands-on support.
  • Own BigQuery at Spotify scale: Manage reservations and capacity, build monitoring and anti-pattern detection, and develop tooling like the BigQuery MCP server so teams can use BigQuery well.
  • Keep the platform healthy: Take part in a weekly support rotation and shared on-call. You'll debug production issues that span storage formats, catalog APIs, Kubernetes reconciliation, GCP IAM and BigQuery internals, and you'll automate away recurring toil.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    We also own BigQuery for all of Spotify. Thousands of engineers, data scientists and pipelines depend on it every day, which puts us on the critical path for storing, finding and querying data.     Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next.

    These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide.

    This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.

     

    ","id":"186b763a-2a61-4563-8813-ff6b40c9c8a7","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Build and Evolve Core Services: Design, build and operate the backend services and APIs behind our data catalog, lineage and publishing systems, and evolve them as the platform adopts new storage technologies and new kinds of data. Hold them to a high bar for correctness, performance and reliability.
  • Build Data Pipelines: Develop and run the batch and streaming pipelines that keep our metadata current, processing platform events and audit logs to capture how data is created and changed, and turning lineage and metadata into data products other teams build on.
  • Own Projects End to End: Turn what the teams using our platform need into technical designs, drive them through delivery and rollout, and own the results once they're in production.
  • Keep the Platform Healthy: Take part in on-call for critical services, build in observability and quality checks by default, and use automation, including AI tooling, to reduce toil for the team and our users.

  • Shape and execute an integrated communications strategy for MENAT+, putting regional creators, audiences, and culture at the heart of Spotify’s storytelling.
  • Be a trusted communications partner to regional leadership, providing clear counsel on business priorities, reputation, emerging issues, and high-impact moments.
  • Anticipate reputational opportunities and risks and help Spotify respond thoughtfully and effectively as cultural, media, policy, and regulatory dynamics evolve.
  • Lead creator-first and earned-first storytelling that builds fandom, discovery, and cultural relevance, finding compelling stories in emerging scenes, communities, and moments that matter locally.
  • Partner with Music, Podcasts, Product, Growth, Marketing, Public Affairs, and other teams to develop communications that support Spotify’s regional priorities.

  • Lead corporate, executive, internal, and B2B communications, including executive positioning, thought leadership, media engagement, and strategic messaging.

  • Own the architecture of Spotify’s subscription portfolio, including tier structure, add-ons, bundles, and how features are allocated across them.
  • Set the logic of the price ladder, including relative pricing, upgrade paths, and how regional ladders work across developed and emerging markets.
  • Drive the insight agenda with Consumer Insights and Analytics, shaping hypotheses, sequencing research, and translating findings into clear portfolio strategy recommendations.
  • Partner with GTM Enablement and cross-functional teams to design, read, and apply in-market tests that connect consumer research with real behavior.
  • Build the business case for portfolio decisions, including sizing, contribution logic, trade-offs, and long-term commercial impact.
  • Drive alignment across Product, Finance, Pricing, Legal, Licensing, and senior leadership on key architecture decisions.
  • Influence the product roadmap so what gets built reflects willingness-to-pay signals, consumer needs, and portfolio strategy.
  • Own the multi-year evolution of Spotify’s subscription portfolio, including where the portfolio should sit two-to-three years out and the sequence of moves to get there.

    Are you passionate about combating fraud, safeguarding revenue, and protecting users from sophisticated threats? As Spotify continues to grow and innovate, we are looking for a dedicated Fraud Analyst to join our Revenue Protection Operations team. In this role, you will play a crucial role in enhancing our fraud prevention strategy—ensuring a proactive balance between user growth, revenue protection, and maintaining a safe, scalable platform.

    With scale comes complexity. You will focus on tackling payment fraud, chargebacks/disputes, creator onboarding and platform misuse that risks revenue leakage and partner trust. 

    As a 12-month cover, you will seamlessly step into our ongoing operations, keeping our momentum strong while bringing fresh perspectives to our workflows. You will work with a global team of world-class business managers, data scientists, product managers, and engineers to build robust operational defenses. If you have a keen eye for detail, strong analytical skills, and a drive to stay one step ahead of fraudsters using cutting-edge technologies, we want to hear from you!

    ","id":"5992c673-e493-48b1-bb63-9b82a4c31876","lists":[{"text":"What You’ll Do","content":"

  • Detection & Mitigation: Review suspicious activity flagged by our fraud systems and take swift mitigating and preventative action to protect our genuine users, secure our growth, and minimize revenue leakage.

  • AI & Tooling Innovation: Actively utilize, test, and adopt emerging AI technologies and automated tooling to enhance fraud detection and improve operational productivity.

  • Build & Optimize: Partner closely with internal Product and Engineering teams as well as external vendors to help contribute to the design, requirement gathering, and testing of tooling and system changes to capture evolving fraud and abuse trends early.

  • Trend Analysis & Investigation: Be creative and proactively seek out new fraud and misuse trends. Present data-informed findings and retrospectives to suggest robust performance guardrails.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Handle daily fraud and misuse escalations while working closely with Data Science, Engineering, and Product teams to translate operational insights into risk mitigation frameworks.

  • Operational Excellence: Support the Revenue Protection leadership in maintaining and improving internal policies, process automation, evidence handling, and operational playbooks.

    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

  • Experience: 2+ years of experience in a fraud analyst or revenue protection role, preferably within an e-commerce, merchant fraud, or creator & marketplace platform environment. Given the fixed-term nature of this role, the ability to rapidly adapt and hit the ground running is highly valued.

  • Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with common fraud prevention techniques, dispute/chargeback management, financial crime risks, and emerging industry trends.

    In this role, you’ll drive demand capture and retention for Premium India by localising global strategies, developing India-specific initiatives, and executing across conversion funnels, offers, lifecycle programs, and win-back initiatives.     ","id":"785d6398-f58b-430c-b300-7928d1d2f9f6","lists":[{"text":"What You’ll Do","content":"

    • Localise and execute the Premium demand capture strategy for India, adapting global frameworks and developing India-specific offer strategies and organic conversion opportunities in collaboration with global and regional Growth teams.

    • Drive programs that reduce voluntary and involuntary churn, anticipating retention risks and developing initiatives to retain and win back users.

    • Own CRM execution using in-house tools to build, manage, and optimise communication journeys across email, push, and in-app channels to improve conversion and retention.

    • Develop and test new conversion and retention approaches, bringing fresh thinking to how we turn free users into Premium subscribers and keep them engaged.

    • Analyse conversion and retention data to identify funnel drop-offs and cohort-specific opportunities, translating insights into clear recommendations and business cases.

    • Design and run A/B tests and experiments across the funnel and CRM channels to improve conversion and subscriber lifetime value.

    • Collaborate with Marketing to connect conversion programs with top-of-funnel activity and key brand moments, and partner with Finance to model offer economics, forecast subscriber growth, and evaluate investment returns.

    • Capture and share learnings that strengthen the Premium Growth playbook, contribute to global best practices, and support cross-regional Growth initiatives when business priorities require it.

    • Integrate AI-driven tools and workflows thoughtfully to improve decision-making and execution efficiency.

  • Coordinate litigation, pre-litigation, regulatory, and other dispute matters across multiple practice areas, including copyright and patent litigation.
  • Work with outside counsel to develop case strategy, manage budgets, and drive efficient resolution of contentious disputes.
  • Partner with the business on litigation and legal risk issues and work with colleagues to fashion solutions that balance legal risk with company objectives.
  • Develop litigation case strategies, work closely with Spotify's communications team, and formulate plans to resolve disputes efficiently.
  • Plan strategically and coordinate internally with legal and non-legal personnel on issues of the moment.
  • Provide proactive advice to internal team members on dispute avoidance and resolution, including risk mitigation.
  • Identify and mitigate threats against the company, whether from partners, users, content owners, or others.
  • Handle requests for information from the company, including subpoenas and requests from law enforcement.
  • Build scalable processes to address a growing number of claims across copyright, patent, and other areas.
  • Train teams and draft workflows and policies to help establish effective internal risk mitigation procedures.
  • Stay current on developments in patent and copyright law, particularly as they affect the technology and media industries.

    Spotify's Content Business team helps bring compelling audio and video content to audiences around the world. Working across Spotify Originals, The Ringer, and licensed content, the team partners with creators, production companies, and internal stakeholders to bring content opportunities to life.

    We're looking for a Manager, Content Acquisition to help turn content opportunities into completed deals. You'll manage the deal process from agreed commercial terms through contract execution, working closely with Legal, Finance, Studios, and external partners. This role combines commercial judgment, contract management, and financial analysis to support Spotify's growing content business.

    ","id":"da45648b-3b35-4e4b-81df-31667aa4a76d","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Manage the execution of original and licensed content deals, from agreed commercial terms through final contracts, signatures, and close.

    • Review, draft, and coordinate revisions to production, licensing, and talent agreements in partnership with Legal.

    • Keep deals moving by tracking progress, identifying outstanding issues, and coordinating next steps with internal teams and external partners.

    • Prepare clear deal documentation, including term sheets, deal summaries, approval materials, and stakeholder updates.

    • Partner with Studios, Finance, Advertising, Partnerships, and Legal to resolve commercial questions and complete agreements.

    • Support the evaluation of new content opportunities through financial models, business cases, and presentations.

    • Monitor content budgets and financial commitments, identify differences against forecasts, and share insights to support informed decisions.

    • Build productive relationships with talent representatives, production companies, and rights holders throughout the deal execution process.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 2+ years of experience in entertainment, media, digital content, business affairs, content acquisition, or deal operations.

    • You understand content licensing, production agreements, and the commercial considerations involved in developing and distributing audio or video content.

    • You're comfortable reviewing term sheets and contracts, identifying key issues, and working with Legal to resolve them.

    • You can manage multiple deals and deadlines while keeping stakeholders informed and maintaining accurate records.

    • You have experience with financial analysis, budget tracking, or financial modeling and can turn data into practical recommendations.

    • You communicate clearly and can explain complex commercial terms to colleagues with different areas of expertise.

    • You enjoy working collaboratively with creative, commercial, legal, and finance teams to solve problems and move projects forward.

    • You bring sound judgment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to managing priorities in a changing environment.

","description":"

    Spotify’s Propositions team is responsible for what we offer and how we package it — the plans, tiers, and propositions that shape how hundreds of millions of people experience and pay for Spotify. As Manager - Proposition Strategy, you’ll help define how Spotify grows its next billion users by developing affordable, locally relevant propositions, evolving existing tiers, and identifying new opportunities that can unlock sustainable growth.

    This is a role for someone who thinks in business cases as much as ideas. You’ll take work from an initial hypothesis through to an executive-ready recommendation — building the economics, assessing margin and licensing implications, modeling cannibalization risk, and creating a clear narrative for senior leaders. You’ll work closely with Strategy, Finance, Product, Legal, and Market teams, and your work will directly influence the propositions Spotify brings to some of the world’s fastest-growing markets.

    ","id":"8251142e-f213-45df-89a9-914e814bd7a7","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Develop new proposition opportunities and evolve existing subscription tiers, grounding recommendations in strong commercial thinking and local market realities.
  • Own the full journey from initial hypothesis to executive recommendation, including opportunity sizing, unit economics, margin and licensing analysis, cannibalization modeling, and the final narrative.
  • Build and stress-test business cases that account for Spotify’s licensing structure, local market dynamics, currency considerations, and subscriber economics.
  • Identify and quantify potential cannibalization across existing tiers and revenue streams, including the relationship between free, lower-cost, and standard offerings in price-sensitive markets.
  • Partner closely with Finance, Product, Legal, Strategy, and Market teams to challenge assumptions, build alignment, and shape clear recommendations.
  • Monitor competitive, consumer, and macroeconomic developments to identify opportunities and risks that should inform the proposition roadmap.
  • Turn complex analysis into clear choices and recommendations that help senior leaders make informed decisions.

  • You understand the dynamics of high-growth consumer markets and have experience working across different markets or geographies.

    We are seeking Research Scientists (across all levels of seniority) to join our Artist-First AI Music Lab. Our team pioneers and advances state-of-the-art generative technologies for music that create breakthrough experiences for fans and artists. We invent entirely new listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:

    • Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We’ll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.
    • Choice in participation: We recognize there’s a wide range of views on the use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.
    • Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for the use of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.
    • Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will leverage our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    Learn more in our press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:
  • Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users.
  • Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences.
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges.
  • Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization.
  • Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field. Previous industry experience is helpful.
  • You have experience in one or more of the following fields: generative modeling, machine learning, music information retrieval, speech processing, audio processing, signal processing, probabilistic modeling, computer vision, or related areas.
  • You have deep expertise in at least one of the focus areas above—whether that's vocal/speech synthesis, post-training alignment techniques (e.g., PPO, GRPO, DPO), or audio-to-audio generation and text-guided music editing.
  • You have publications at leading conferences such as ICASSP, ISMIR, INTERSPEECH, ICLR, AAAI, IJCAI, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, or related venues.
  • You have strong coding skills in Python, PyTorch, and NumPy.
  • You are a creative problem solver who is passionate about building outstanding products that add real value to millions of people.
  • You are enthusiastic about turning research ideas into products operating at scale.
  • You can explain complex topics in simple terms, and you enjoy building strong relationships with colleagues and stakeholders.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

     

    Security engineers at Spotify protect our platform, employees, creators, and more than 700 million users. We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer to join the Detection and Response organization and help identify, investigate, and respond to threats across Spotify's environment.

     

    You will work within our detection engineering squad where the team owns alert triage, security investigations, threat hunting, and the detection engineering lifecycle. You will turn threat intelligence, incident learnings, and analyst feedback into effective detections and investigation workflows. You will partner closely with the detection infrastructure squad, which builds and operates Detection and Response platforms and telemetry pipelines, and with teams across Spotify to make sure your squad has the signals and capabilities needed to detect and respond to threats at Spotify's scale.

     

    We are a distributed team that values curiosity, sound judgment, clear communication, and continuous learning. We teach and learn from one another, adapt as the threat landscape changes, and focus our effort according to business needs and risk.

    ","id":"cb29d857-395b-401d-9749-367e666ff870","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Identify detection opportunities, define clear telemetry requirements, and partner with the detection infrastructure squad and data owners to make the signals needed for detection and investigation available.

    • Develop, test, tune, and maintain detections across endpoint, identity, cloud, SaaS, email, and other security-relevant environments.

    • Investigate and prioritize alerts, determine their security impact, and participate in incident containment and remediation.

    • Build repeatable investigation workflows and playbooks for alert triage, evidence collection, decision-making, escalation, containment, and response.

    • Improve proactive threat-identification and threat-hunting capabilities using internal telemetry and external threat intelligence.

    • Create cutting-edge AI workflows for Detection and Response that enrich alerts, gather and analyze evidence, guide investigations, and automate repetitive response work while preserving appropriate human judgment and oversight.

    • Measure detection effectiveness, identify coverage gaps, and tune detections to balance security value, fidelity, and analyst workload.

    • Use SIEM, EDR, SOAR, and related security platforms to research threats, develop detections, investigate alerts, and validate security outcomes.

    • Share knowledge, document decisions, and communicate security findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You are curious, collaborative, and comfortable making progress in an ambiguous and rapidly changing environment.

    • You have 3+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, threat detection, detection engineering, or closely related work.

    • You understand how analysts triage and investigate alerts and how detection quality affects their decisions and workload.

    • You know how to create and tune detections based on attacker behavior, available telemetry, and an expected investigation path.

    • You are experienced with security platforms such as SIEM, EDR, SOAR, or comparable monitoring and response technologies.

    • You can write code or use an automation platform to analyze security telemetry, enrich alerts, build investigation workflows, and remove repetitive work. Experience with Python or a similar language is valuable.

    • You understand modern detection-as-code practices, including GitHub, peer review, CI/CD, testing, and safely managing production detection content.

    • You have experience working with at least one major cloud platform, such as Google Cloud, AWS, or Azure.

    • You understand common threats affecting SaaS-oriented corporate and production environments.

    • You care about clear documentation, inclusive collaboration, and explaining security concepts to people with different backgrounds and levels of expertise.

    • You are excited to create and critically evaluate cutting-edge AI workflows for detection development, alert triage, security investigations, and response, while applying sound security judgment and appropriate human oversight.

    "},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

    • This role is based in New York

    We’re looking for a Senior C++/iOS Engineer to join the Baldur squad within User Platform (UP). Baldur owns Spotify’s Session Management and Delegated Authorization domains—the systems that enable applications to securely obtain, use, and manage access tokens for hundreds of millions of users. In this role, you’ll help shape the technology that powers secure access across every Spotify client and third-party integration. 

    Your work will support engineers across Spotify building mobile and desktop experiences, platform teams, and third-party developers integrating with Spotify’s authorization platform.   • Collaborate with a highly autonomous and supportive engineering squad responsible for Spotify’s delegated authorization and session management platforms.
  • Design, build, and evolve critical infrastructure powering Spotify applications and partner integrations using shared C++ libraries and native Swift on iOS.
  • Develop secure, reliable, and performant delegated authorization flows, including token issuance, refresh, revocation, and session lifecycle management across multiple platforms.
  • Partner with client and backend engineers to integrate with core authorization services, token issuance, client registration, and token revocation.
  • Improve how credentials and access tokens are securely stored and managed on-device while balancing security, reliability, and application performance.
  • Contribute to the evolution of Spotify’s authorization frameworks, Spotify-specific implementations, enabling new platforms and product experiences.
  • Drive technical improvements, share knowledge with teammates, and help shape the long-term technical direction of delegated authorization and session management.

    We’re looking for a Senior Digital Learning Experience Designer to join our Learning & Inclusion team, the group responsible for creating learning experiences that help every Spotify band member grow, belong, and do their best work.

    You’ll bring together instructional design, visual design, storytelling, and broader learning and development expertise to create inclusive and effective experiences at scale. You’ll partner with subject-matter experts, people leaders, and Learning & Inclusion colleagues on company-wide initiatives, from leadership development to programs that bring Spotify’s values to life.

    ","id":"9d1c90b5-a8a4-4218-b2f3-7bbaefae7fd1","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead the end-to-end design of learning experiences, from needs analysis and curriculum architecture through development, launch, and evaluation.
  • Partner with subject-matter experts and stakeholders to identify performance needs and turn them into clear learning objectives and practical solutions.
  • Design learning journeys across live, digital, blended, and self-directed formats using evidence-based learning principles.
  • Create engaging learning materials, including eLearning, facilitator guides, participant resources, job aids, presentations, and micro-learning experiences.
  • Use visual design and storytelling to make complex ideas clear, memorable, and engaging while creating experiences that feel unmistakably Spotify.
  • Build interactive digital learning experiences using AI-assisted workflows and authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline or Rise, Adobe Captivate, or similar platforms.
  • Design inclusive learning experiences that reflect different perspectives, reduce barriers to participation, and support a culture of belonging.
  • Pilot and iterate on learning experiences using learner feedback, stakeholder input, and performance data.
  • Define meaningful measures of success and evaluate learning effectiveness, knowledge transfer, learner experience, and behavior change.
  • Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Explore emerging approaches in learning design, including AI-assisted authoring and adaptive learning, and apply them where they can meaningfully improve the learner experience.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have 5+ years of professional instructional design experience and a portfolio demonstrating thoughtful work across multiple learning formats.
  • You apply learning science principles such as cognitive load, retrieval practice, spaced learning, and adult learning theory to practical design decisions.
  • You know how to uncover learning and performance needs, translate them into measurable objectives, and design learning journeys that build knowledge and skills over time.
  • You create meaningful practice through scenarios, simulations, assessments, and other interactive experiences rather than relying on passive content.
  • You have strong visual and UX design judgment and understand how typography, hierarchy, layout, and visual storytelling can make learning clearer and easier to navigate.
  • You have experience with rapid authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Captivate, Lectora, or similar platforms, along with design tools such as Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or equivalent.
  • You can create clear storyboards, scripts, facilitator guides, and supporting materials that help others confidently deliver consistent learning experiences.
  • You use learner feedback and data to evaluate effectiveness, iterate on your work, and connect learning experiences to meaningful outcomes.
  • You communicate complex ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with subject-matter experts, leaders, and cross-functional partners.
  • You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing multiple priorities, and taking ownership from an early idea through a polished learning experience.
  • You bring experience in areas such as inclusive learning design, leadership development, learning technology, short-form learning video or animation, LMS/LXP platforms, or SCORM/xAPI.
  • You have a degree in instructional design, learning sciences, education, human-computer interaction, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

    ","id":"c114627b-1306-4581-95a8-77d847ee9962","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead and develop Engineering Managers across multiple teams, supporting their growth while creating clarity around outcomes and engineering excellence.
  • Set and communicate engineering strategy across the studio, ensuring teams have clear technical direction aligned with IT’s mandate and Spotify’s business needs.
  • Strengthen technical judgment across the Engineering Manager group, challenging processes that no longer add value and creating more space for architecture, quality, and team capability.
  • Identify patterns and opportunities across teams and drive improvements in engineering practice, operational health, reliability, and ways of working.
  • Establish and evolve engineering best practices across the studio, helping teams share knowledge and consistently improve how we build and operate technology.
  • Champion reliability, security, compliance, and privacy as fundamental parts of engineering decision-making.
  • Shape how AI is used across the company, both through the tools our squads build and how our engineers work day to day.
  • Partner with studio and alliance leadership, procurement, legal, engineering counterparts, and teams across Spotify to make thoughtful technical investments and solve meaningful business problems.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have 8+ years of engineering experience and experience leading Engineering Managers across multiple teams.
  • You have led engineering organisations at scale and can demonstrate how the technical strategies you’ve shaped have influenced meaningful outcomes.
  • You bring experience with enterprise technology such as identity and access, SaaS platforms, endpoint management, workplace technology, architecture, or related systems, and can engage credibly in technical decisions across these areas.
  • You have improved engineering practices across multiple teams and know how to balance developer productivity, operational excellence, reliability, and sustainable technical investment.
  • You have developed Engineering Managers into stronger leaders and can point to meaningful growth and progression within the teams you’ve led.

    You will contribute your expertise to various music-related projects within the company, including playlist curation, creative editorial work, and cross-functional collaboration with different teams in the region and beyond. You will provide deep cultural and musical insights to create highly engaging and cohesive music experiences for listeners, extending beyond playlists, while ensuring an unbiased editorial voice for a wide array of moods, moments, and genres. Additionally, you will drive artist discovery through an extensive editorial ecosystem of playlists and tools, critically assessing music trends and user behavior to identify opportunities and emerging trends.

    You will demonstrate a team player spirit, a passion for performance-oriented analytics, and a solid understanding of Spotify’s role in the music industry both locally and globally. Additionally, you will have an editorial personality that thrives in engaging audiences through creative formats, bringing the playlists to life in innovative ways.

    ","id":"a57db22d-dc0d-4f36-9a2e-34acdf1ec046","lists":[{"text":"What You Will Do","content":"
  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for how free users become aware of, experience, and develop intent for Premium, driving consideration, conversion intent, and subscriber growth across segments and markets.
  • Lead the discovery, design, and delivery of subscriber-facing features from early concept through global rollout.
  • Drive experiments that deepen our understanding of what makes users want Premium and measurably move free users closer to a purchase decision.
  • Turn behavioral, funnel, and market data into clear hypotheses, define meaningful success metrics, and build a prioritized experimentation roadmap.
  • Design rigorous A/B experiments to evaluate funnel changes against strong baselines, scaling approaches that demonstrably work across markets and segments.
  • Make pragmatic trade-offs across user value, revenue impact, regional nuance, and operational complexity, knowing when a simple flow change is enough and when a deeper platform capability is needed.
  • Partner with marketing, research, and regional teams to adapt value positioning and messaging for different markets, competitive landscapes, and user needs, including high-growth emerging markets where the path to Premium may look fundamentally different.
  • Communicate strategy, results, and trade-offs clearly to senior stakeholders, translating funnel mechanics and subscription economics into business impact and strategic direction.

","description":"

    We are looking for a Senior Revenue Operations Analyst to support Spotify’s global Order-to-Cash operations and revenue close process. You’ll work at the intersection of accounting and operations, helping ensure accurate financial reporting while building processes and systems that can scale with our business.

    In this role, you’ll partner across Finance, Engineering, Tax, Sales, and other teams to solve complex operational challenges, strengthen our revenue processes, and support Spotify’s continued growth.

    ","id":"8c8c3cfc-4156-4dad-bb6d-48266766e94a","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Support the monthly and quarterly revenue close, including journal entries, revenue accruals, deferrals, and manual adjustments in accordance with IFRS
  • Prepare and review complex balance sheet reconciliations across statutory books and consolidated ledgers, and analyze month-end movements across revenue, deferred revenue, accounts receivable, and related accounts
  • Manage global e-invoicing operations across subsidiaries, partnering with Tax to understand local requirements and resolve invoice delivery, data, and validation issues
  • Support day-to-day global Order-to-Cash operations, including manual billing and accounts receivable activities
  • Maintain strong financial controls and support SOX, ITGC, and internal and external audit requirements
  • Identify operational bottlenecks and partner with IT and Financial Engineering to design, test, and implement system enhancements, automated workflows, and controls
  • Collaborate with Legal, Sales, Sales Operations, FP&A, Tax, Technical Accounting, and other partners on revenue policies, programs, and strategic initiatives
  • Mentor and support accounting team members and external vendor partners, while contributing to operational metrics, integrations, and special projects
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You have 4+ years of experience across revenue accounting, revenue operations, general ledger accounting, public accounting, or a related area, along with a bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or equivalent experience
  • You have a strong understanding of the full Order-to-Cash lifecycle and core accounting concepts, including accruals, deferrals, multi-entity or multi-currency accounting, reconciliations, and month-end close
  • You have experience executing or troubleshooting e-invoicing workflows in a global, multi-entity environment
  • You are comfortable working with ERP and billing systems such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or comparable platforms
  • You have strong Excel and analytical skills and are comfortable working with large, complex datasets; experience with SQL, BigQuery, or data visualization tools is valuable

    Spotify's Global Organic Social team shapes how Spotify connects with audiences across its owned social channels, bringing fans closer to the music, podcasts, audiobooks, and experiences they love.

    We're looking for a Social Strategy Manager to help grow and engage communities around podcasts, books, and fitness on Spotify. You'll develop social strategies that celebrate creators, connect with fans, and bring cultural moments to life, from major podcast releases and book launches to fitness experiences.

    As part of our Global Organic Social team, you'll work with Creative, Communications, Marketing, Partnerships, and other teams to turn business priorities into compelling, platform-native social campaigns. You'll balance long-term strategy with timely cultural opportunities, using creative judgment, audience insights, and performance data to shape work that makes an impact.

    ","id":"d9e57c3c-1c0a-483b-a783-6d1c9f2ce057","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Lead organic social strategy for high-impact campaigns, creator partnerships, and cultural moments across Spotify's podcasts, books, and fitness experiences, from initial planning through launch and evaluation.

    • Turn integrated marketing objectives into creative, platform-native social strategies that engage audiences, strengthen fandoms, and support business goals.

    • Manage complex social campaigns across internal teams and agency partners, coordinating briefs, timelines, creative development, approvals, and delivery.

    • Partner with Creative, Communications, Marketing, Product, Content Partnerships, Paid Media, Legal, and external agencies to develop integrated campaigns and culturally relevant social experiences.

    • Identify emerging audience behaviors, creator trends, and cultural opportunities, developing proactive social programming that keeps Spotify and its creators connected with fans between major campaigns.

    • Shape social creative and content capture strategies for podcasts, long-form video, live events, and experiential activations, providing clear direction and actionable feedback to creative and production partners.

    • Develop social strategy frameworks and best practices, sharing recommendations with cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders to strengthen how Spotify approaches organic social marketing.

    • Define campaign success metrics alongside analytics partners, evaluate performance, and turn audience insights into recommendations that improve future campaigns and ongoing social programming.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 7+ years of experience in organic social media strategy, social marketing, or a related role within consumer, entertainment, technology, or media brands.

    • You have experience developing social strategies for integrated marketing campaigns, balancing business objectives, audience needs, and platform-native creative ideas.

    The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

    Surfaces Moments is a ML team within the Personalization Mission focused on creating moment-based experiences across Spotify surfaces. The team owns and evolves the experiences that help listeners quickly connect with the content that matters most to them, including the Home Shortcuts experience and the underlying intelligence that powers it. By combining cutting-edge machine learning, recommendation systems, and product thinking, the team delivers highly relevant, personalized experiences to millions of listeners around the world.

    As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of recommendation systems, large language models, and production-scale machine learning infrastructure to build experiences that delight users and drive meaningful impact. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys taking models from research to production, driving technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces, and solving complex personalization challenges at global scale.

    ","id":"281e7db9-86ba-4a1c-8773-c23b96ed32dc","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Own and improve the machine learning models and systems that power the Home feed, including the Shortcuts experience.

    • Design, build, and ship personalized recommendations that serve millions of Spotify listeners globally.

    • Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences.

    • Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches.

    • Partner closely with product managers, engineers, data scientists, and designers to define and execute experimentation strategies.

    • Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency.

    • Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale.

    • Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of personalization systems.

    • Mentor and support other machine learning engineers, helping raise the bar across the team.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have 8+ years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production environments.

    • You have deep expertise in recommendation systems, ranking models, personalization, or large-scale content discovery platforms.

    • You have strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience building machine learning systems with PyTorch.

    • You are experienced with large language model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and optimization techniques including SFT, distillation, and LoRA.

    • You have worked with large-scale inference systems and understand the challenges of latency, reliability, and cost optimization.

    • You care deeply about creating high-quality user experiences through thoughtful application of machine learning.

    • You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, and you influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team

    • You know how to design, execute, and interpret online experiments and A/B tests to improve user outcomes.

    • You have experience operating distributed machine learning workloads using technologies such as Ray, FSDP, HSDP, or similar frameworks.

    • You are experienced building and maintaining data pipelines and orchestration workflows using technologies such as Flyte, Airflow, BigQuery, and cloud-based storage platforms.

    "},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

    • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location.

    • This team operates within the Eastern Standard time zone for collaboration.

    We are currently looking for a new band member to join the Spotify Tax Team. This new band member will be an Analyst, joining the Global Indirect Tax Team. This position will report into the Senior Manager for Indirect Tax in EMEA and APAC and will be based in Stockholm, Sweden.

    In your role, you will focus on compliance and reporting. Spotify reports indirect taxes in more than 90 countries globally and you will be a key member of the team responsible for ensuring the completeness, timeliness and accuracy of Spotify’s global indirect tax compliance obligations. You will work in close collaboration with global tax team members in both Stockholm and New York, and work cross functionally with various accounting and finance teams.

    We are a team of highly skilled and dedicated colleagues and we offer a challenging and dynamic role in an ever changing environment with the opportunity to take on much responsibility in a rapidly growing international company. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences audio.
